pred_reasoning_trace: A 55-year-old man with no significant medical history presented with a 10-month history of spontaneous, progressively painful umbilical discomfort. A few days after the onset of pain, he noted a firm nodule at the umbilicus that gradually increased in size and became ulcerated and tender. On examination, he was in good general condition. The umbilical lesion measured 6 cm by 6 cm, was ulcerated over its entire surface, and bled on contact. Deep palpation of the abdomen revealed a poorly defined, firm mass approximately 8 cm in diameter in the right hypochondrium. Biopsy of the umbilical lesion demonstrated a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed homogeneously enhancing umbilical tissue growth and irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon measuring approximately 8.3 cm. Total colonoscopy revealed no endoluminal lesion.
